ios-patterns|Drag and drop.summary: Drag and drop on iOS keeps the system’s own drag: a long press lifts the item with the system preview, items move within and between lists and apps, and VoiceOver offers the same moves as custom actions. Plenix styles what the app draws around it: the lifted row on the raised surface with the overlay shadow, the insertion line and the drop target’s dashed outline in the focus ring’s color, a refusing target in the danger color with words, and a Move menu (and Move up, Move down in an edited list) so every drag has a way without dragging. Apple’s default is the system preview over the app’s own unstyled targets; Plenix keeps the system gesture and preview and replaces the app’s look.

anatomy.name: Drag handle
anatomy.about: The grip at the row’s start in an edited list (the system reorder control), or the whole item lifted by a long press.

anatomy.name: Lifted item
anatomy.about: The item under the finger on the raised surface with the overlay shadow; the system preview when it leaves the app.

anatomy.name: Insertion line
anatomy.about: A line in the focus ring’s color where the item lands in a list.

anatomy.name: Drop target
anatomy.about: A dashed outline in the focus ring’s color and the hover fill while an item it takes is over it; the danger color and words when it refuses.

anatomy.name: Move menu
anatomy.about: Move up, Move down, Move to … in the item’s context menu and as VoiceOver custom actions: the way without dragging.
